builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: To Reason but Not to Stop: Understanding and Recovering Pruned Large Reasoning Models
summary: TGAS replaces retraining or abandoning pruned reasoning models by adding a learned-free, training-free steering direction to the residual stream at inference time to restore termination behavior. It costs a one-time extraction of a hidden-state direction from terminating versus looping continuations plus a small per-token activation addition, with negligible memory and latency overhead. It can fail if the shared termination direction does not transfer to a new pruning recipe, model, or domain, and it only recovers accuracy lost to non-termination, leaving any genuine reasoning degradation from pruning unaddressed.
rationale: The reader can apply this training-free inference-time patch on a single GPU if they deploy pruned reasoning models, but the benefit is specific to sparsity-induced looping and must be validated on their exact checkpoints and workloads.

claims.statement: TGAS replaces retraining or abandoning pruned reasoning models by adding a learned-free, training-free steering direction to the residual stream at inference time to restore termination behavior. It costs a one-time extraction of a hidden-state direction from terminating versus looping continuations plus a small per-token activation addition, with negligible memory and latency overhead. It can fail if the shared termination direction does not transfer to a new pruning recipe, model, or domain, and it only recovers accuracy lost to non-termination, leaving any genuine reasoning degradation from pruning unaddressed.

Across six LRMs, three pruning pipelines, and math and code benchmarks, TGAS improves termination and overall accuracy while reducing repetitive reasoning and generation length; no single quantified figure is given in the abstract.
